claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'm happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To give you an accurate assessment, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you applying Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to apply for Child Benefit for my son Alex. So just the one child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'm assessing your eligibility for Child Benefit for your son, Alex.

Before I can give you a proper answer, I need to understand a bit more about your circumstances. Let me ask you some questions to check the eligibility criteria.

**First, how old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Next, does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, yes and no - it's a bit complicated. He does live with me, but his other parent lives with us too and they already claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

Before I can give you a final decision, I need to check the specific rules about this situation. Let me read the relevant guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on the guidance I've reviewed, I now have a clear picture of your situation.

According to the Child Benefit rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. The guidance states: "Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit."

Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex as well. Only one person can receive Child Benefit payments for any given child.

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time, because his other parent is already claiming for him. The key rule here is that **only one person can receive Child Benefit for any child** – two people cannot both claim for the same child.

If you wish to be the person claiming Child Benefit for Alex instead of his other parent, you would need to arrange this with his other parent. One of you would need to stop claiming, and the other would need to be the sole claimant. You can contact the Child Benefit Office to discuss changing who claims for Alex if that's something you'd like to explore.
